gloss: one's legs are worn out (from walking or standing)

definitions.gloss: to have legs as stiff as sticks; to be worn out from walking
definitions.explanation: Literally "one's legs become sticks": after a long time walking or standing, the legs are so tired they feel stiff and heavy. Almost always in the past tense, describing how one ended up.

examples.english: My legs are completely worn out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一日中|いちにちじゅう}→一日中：09519_ichinichijuu⟧⟦{歩|ある}き{回|まわ}って→歩き回る：04605_arukimawaru⟧、{足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になった。
examples.english: I walked around all day and my legs are dead.

examples.japanese: ⟦{立|た}ち→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧⟦っぱなし→〜っぱなし：33296_ppanashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧で、⟦{夕方|ゆうがた}→夕方：01010_yuugata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{棒|ぼう}→棒：03726_bou⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: My job keeps me on my feet, so by evening my legs always feel like sticks.

notes:
Conjugates like ⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: {足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になった, {足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になる⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk until one's legs give out). The variant ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{棒|ぼう}→棒：03726_bou⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ says the same thing as a simile.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になる⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{探|さが}す→探す：00493_sagasu⟧: to search until one can hardly walk
- ⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧すぎて{足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になる: to walk one's legs off

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦くたくた→くたくた：05169_kutakuta⟧: worn out all over, not only the legs
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つる: to get a cramp in the leg; a sudden pain, not tiredness
